Commentary.Commentary: So that is it from this game. South Africa take the lead in this 3-match ODI series and spoil the world champions comeback in ODIs. England will look to put this loss behind and bounce back stronger. South Africa will look to wrap up the series in the second ODI. The second ODI will be played on Friday, 7th February. That match will begin at 1300 local (1100 GMT). Join us for that one. Till then, cheers!

For his superb knock of 107 South African skipper is also the Man of the Match. De Kock says that it was a good night and says he is glad to get back to winning ways. Says they had chats about how they want to take the ODI team forward and today was the beginning of it. On spinners, he says it is good to have two spinners, especially Smuts as he is an all-rounder. De Kock humbly says that it has just been one game and he hopes that captaincy serves him well.  Adds that the extra responsibility brought the best out of him. Tells him and Bavuma knew running hard between the wickets was the way to go about it and they just tried to carry the momentum.

England skipper, Morgan says they were completely outplayed by South Africa and admits that they misread the condition. Tells everyone struggled with the bat except Woakes and Denly. Credits South Africa for starting the series well and says South Africa bowled better and executed better than they did. Says they lost wickets in clusters and the total was only good if they would have been able to manage to pick wickets regularly. Tells the new guys learnt a lot and adds they saw that it is not all crash and bang like T20. Says they need to continue to learn like how they did in the past.

Earlier in the day after being put into bat, England were in tatters at 131/6 but Joe Denly's fighting 87 along with a smart knock of 40 from Woakes gave the tourists something to bowl at and they managed to get to 258. It was a superb bowling performance from South Africa. Tabraiz Shamsi was the star as his 3-fer never let England going and restricted them to an under par score.

A sorry bowling performance from the world champions. They were unable to adjust to the demands of the pitch and had no ideas on how to get rid of de Kock and Bavuma. When they did, it was just too late as the game was already beyond any doubts. Yes, it is not an experienced bowling line-up but England skipper Morgan would have hoped for a better display from them. Three bowlers got into the wickets column. Root, Woakes and Jordan. The latter was expensive as well. Parkinson did not have any success on his debut.

Chasing a moderate total of 259, South Africa were dealt with an early blow as they lost Reeza Hendricks early. Bavuma then joined his skipper and what we saw from the two was just pure masterclass. They took on the English attack. The skipper and his deputy led from the front and the pair added 173 for the second wicket and killed all the English hopes. Quinton de Kock, the skipper scored a century but Bavuma fell 2 runs short of a well-deserved hundred but that did not prove to be costly as van der Dussen applied the finishing touches.

The world champions have been humbled on their first game as champions. England's nightmare at Newlands continues. What a brilliant performance from the Proteas and their life under new leader, Quinton de Kock is off to a comprehensive win. Their sorrows and disappointment from the Test series have been reduced a tad here as they take a 1-0 lead in this 3-match ODI series.

OUT! LBW! Such an anti-climatic end to Temba Bavuma's superb innings. He has to walk out 2 short of what would have been a terrific century. Heartbreak and disappointment for him and for a moment the whole crowd goes very silent. This is a very good ball from Chris Jordan. Very full and very pacy. It is on middle and leg, Bavuma looks to defend but gets beaten by the sheer pace of it. The ball hits his pad and he goes down on the turf. Bavuma refers it upstairs in a desperate hope of survival. Replay rolls in and Ultra Edge shows that there is no bat involved. Time for the Ball Tracker and it shows three reds. No luck for Temba and he has to walk back. End of a terrific knock from him. Deserved a hundred but he will not get it. Can England manage to make a comeback in this game and snatch victory from the jaws of defeat? Looks a bit late but one can never be sure in cricket.

He tempts Reeza to go for a slash, he falls in the trap and goes for it. The ball bounces a bit high and kisses the outside edge of Hendrick's bat. It goes straight to Jonny Bairstow behind the stumps. He is not going to drop those. 234 needed in 258 now.
Good length delivery on off, Hendricks blocks it off the back foot.
On a good length on middle, Hendricks keeps it out.
Full delivery on off, Hendricks drives it towards mid off.
Length delivery on off, Hendricks pushes it towards covers.
On a length on off, de Kock taps it towards point for a single.
Good length delivery on off, Hendricks defends it off the front foot.

On a length on middle, Hendricks flicks it to mid-wicket.
Length delivery on off, de Kock punches it towards point for a single.
Full delivery on middle, de Kock drives it back towards the bowler.

EDGED AND FOUR! Just wide of the keeper. Length delivery just outside off, de Kock looks to cut but gets a thick outside edge. Luckily for the South African skipper, the ball flies past the diving Bairstow and goes to the third man fence.
Length delivery on off, de Kock plays it towards covers for a single.
On a good length on middle, de Kock looks to pull but gets hit on the thigh pad.
Length delivery on off, de Kock plays it towards covers.
On a length on off, Quinton plays it to covers.
On a good length on off, Hendricks looks to defend but gets an outside edge. It goes towards third man for a single.
Length delivery on off, de Kock guides it towards third man for a run.
On a length on middle, Hendricks nudges it to mid-wicket.
FOUR! Excellent shot. Sam is guilty of overpitching it on off, Hendricks gets on his front foot and drives it with class through covers for a boundary.
Full delivery on middle, de Kock drives it past the bowler towards mid on for a single.
Length delivery on off, de Kock plays it to covers.
On a good length on off, de Kock defends it off the back foot.

Length delivery on off, Quinton guides it towards third man for a single.
On a good length on off, de Kock defends it off the front foot.
Length delivery outside off, de Kock punches it through point. The batsmen get two runs.
Full delivery on off, de Kock drives it back towards the bowler.
Again outside off, de Kock leaves it alone.
Good length delivery outside off, de Kock shoulders arms to this one.
Full delivery on middle, de Kock drives it towards mid on for a run.
On a good length on off, Quinton blocks it off the front foot.
Length delivery on off, Hendricks guides it towards third man for a single.

FOUR! First boundary of the chase. Full on off, de Kock drives it straight past the bowler through mid off for a boundary.

OUT, LBW! BUT OVERTURNED! A successful review for South Africa. A length ball around the off pole line, it pitches and comes back in sharply. Hendricks looks to flick this one towards the leg side but misses to get hit on the pads. The England players appeal and up goes the finger. Hendricks cannot believe it and after talking with his partner goes for the review. Ultra Edge comes in and confirms no bat involved. Now comes the Ball Tracker and shows that it is missing the leg pole by a huge margin. The umpire's decision is reversed and Hendricks will play on.
First ball for Hendricks, he has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
South Africa's run chase is underway! Full ball on the pads, flicked towards square leg and the batters take a single.
Length ball this time on the off pole line, angling away, de Kock leaves this one alone.
Good length ball just around the off pole line, de Kock rocks back and defends.
Woakes starts with a full ball around the off pole line, de Kock pushes this one towards the mid off region.
We are back for the chase. The England players are out in the middle. Quinton de Kock and Reeza Hendricks will open the batting for South Africa. Chris Woakes will start the proceedings for England.
